pr_title: Google Assistant SDK: allow credentials from json to allow personal results
pr_body:
## Proposed change
<!--
  Describe the big picture of your changes here to communicate to the
  maintainers why we should accept this pull request. If it fixes a bug
  or resolves a feature request, be sure to link to that issue in the
  additional information section.
-->
Allow users to enable personal results by having /config/google_assistant_sdk_credentials.json created with google-oauthlib-tool on a desktop or laptop with local access. This is needed because for personal results to work the oauth client needs to be of Desktop app instead of Web application. See https://github.com/home-assistant/home-assistant.io/pull/28621 for the steps needed.

These are all the options No I haven't tried the other options: Android, iOS, Chrome Extension, Universal Windows Platform since they would be even harder to get the creds.
But you have tested TVs and limited input devices type? Is there any Google docs about what credentials offer personal results?

There is no documentation. I have not personally tried TV but from others only Desktop app works. See e.g. `https://github.com/Melvin-Abraham/Google-Assistant-Unofficial-Desktop-Client/issues/784#issuecomment-1465096952` and a ton of related discussion in that repo.

I just tried TVs and limited input devices. It didn't work. I got:

Error 400: invalid_request
The loopback flow has been blocked in order to keep users secure. Follow the Loopback IP Address flow migration guide linked in the developer docs below to migrate your app to an alternative method.
[Related developer documentation](https://developers.google.com/identity/protocols/oauth2/resources/loopback-migration)
Automatic token refresh won't work with the credentials file, right? The access token will still expire after a while and will need to be manually refreshed by the user, is that correct?
The credentials file includes the refresh token so the access token is refreshed automatically.

@MartinHjelmare  Thanks for your feedback. What do you think of the following alternatives?

1. Revert all changes and only change `OptionsFlowHandler` in config_flow to let users override the following with values from the output of `google-oauthlib-tool`:
    - `refresh_token` in `core.config_entries`
    - `client_id` and `client_secret` in `application_credentials` in 
2. Abandon this and require users manually messing up with the above files
3. Not require users running `google-oauthlib-tool`. In the config flow after entering the applications credentials (client id + secret) ask them if the type is desktop or web application. If it's desktop, change the host in the `redirect_uri` to `localhost:42735` and ask the user to manually change the host to `homeassistant.local:8123` (or whatever is their instance) in the URL bar of their browser after they complete the authorization steps and get the "This site can't be reached" page when their browser hits the `localhost:42735`.

My preference is 3 since it's easier for the user. If you agree, what's the best approach to implement this? One way is to change `extra_authorize_data` in this integration's config flow to change the `redirect_uri` at two places https://github.com/home-assistant/core/blob/76427a00806197099fc5c15fceb653ea29367036/homeassistant/helpers/config_entry_oauth2_flow.py#L163-L165. The issue is that this would rely on implementation details.

issue_context.title: Google Assistant SDK not managing to get access to personal results
issue_context.body:
### The problem

Trying to set Google reminders using Google Assistant SDK command. I get a notification on my phone to grant permission to access personal results, however toggling it on causes the screen to crash. 
There is no Device name populated. If I do populate a device name I am able to toggle Personal results on but it doesn't save settings.

I suspect this might be because there is no defined Device Name in the API call.

### What version of Home Assistant Core has the issue?

2023.1.0

### What was the last working version of Home Assistant Core?

_No response_

### What type of installation are you running?

Home Assistant OS

### Integration causing the issue

Google Assistant SDK

### Link to integration documentation on our website

https://www.home-assistant.io/integrations/google_assistant_sdk

### Diagnostics information

_No response_

### Example YAML snippet

_No response_

_No response_

This is a known issue mentioned in https://www.home-assistant.io/integrations/google_assistant_sdk#limitationsknown-issues
Using the demo.py of the underlying library I was able to enable personal results by tapping on the notification, renaming the device first and then allowing personal results. However I cannot do the same when I issue a personal query via the integration.

I suspect it's for security reaons on Google's end. The only difference between demo.py, where I got personal results working, and the integration, is in the creds. For the demo I used a localhost redirect but for the integration I used my.home-assistant.io redirect.

really hoping this can be made work in future.

for example the volvo/polestar integration returns results of charge status, is the car locked etc. without being able to see the response we cant make a wrapper module for volvo/polestar

The API that this project uses works just fine.
https://github.com/Melvin-Abraham/Google-Assistant-Unofficial-Desktop-Client.
Which is this:
https://github.com/endoplasmic/google-assistant

It takes a handful of settings on googles side to get it to work, but in the end it does work.

My suspicion earlier was correct.
